gate_reference: MDB.10 / PERFORMANCE_AND_NATIVE_INTEGRATION.md section 3: direct CLI metadata query p95 < 100 ms and local shared-service query p95 < 50 ms on the designated reference machine; this run is on a development host
boundary: per frontend: CLI process start through exit; Python Collection.query including its CLI process; loopback HTTP request through decoded response for vulcan serve with --no-watch (one-shot service) and with watching (retained session)
build: cargo build --release -p vulcan-cli from the commit that adds this file (parent 8df434d8)

host.conditions: uncontrolled power, frequency, and background load

method.percentiles: nearest rank; repeated successful requests only

timing.http_oneshot: loopback request through decoded response (urllib, one connection per request)
timing.http_watched: loopback request through decoded response (urllib, one connection per request)
timing.python: Collection.query call, including its CLI process and JSON decoding

skipped_frontends.http_oneshot: benchmark_public grants no index access, which vulcan serve requires
skipped_frontends.http_watched: benchmark_public grants no index access, which vulcan serve requires

findings: Every measured frontend returned the identical envelope for each of the fixture's nine query cases, unrestricted and under benchmark_public; every response matched the generator's known answer.
The HTTP frontends are within about 1 ms of each other (p95 6.7 ms one-shot, 7.3 ms watched): both serve these queries from the indexed path, and per-request HTTP and permission work is small.

The CLI's p95 (105 ms unrestricted, 112 ms restricted) includes process start, vault discovery, and the blocking freshness check; it is near the 100 ms reference-host target on this slower laptop and is not an acceptance verdict.

The Python wrapper adds a few milliseconds to its CLI process at p50. The first run's p95 of 378 ms did not reproduce: a 300-sample rerun measured p95 116 ms against the CLI's 87 ms, so that tail was host noise.
The first CLI request after `vulcan index scan` took 15.7 s building the mdbase record cache; it is reported separately and excluded from the percentiles.
limitations: Development host, not the designated reference machine; no acceptance verdict
Sequential single-client requests; no concurrent readers or writers

Restricted HTTP was not measured: vulcan serve needs a profile with index access and benchmark_public (part of the fixture digest) has none; vulcan-cli/tests/mdbase_frontends.rs covers restricted HTTP parity
No in-process (route handler) frontend here; note-query-frontends.json measures that boundary
